Emma — putting the pieces together and attaching an initial MAP + sensitivity file. High level notes here so you have a quick summary for procurement: 

- Baseline tokens per call: 750 tokens (average request + response) — this is Lumexa's profile based on the sample transcripts you shared.
- Pricing scenarios (tokens / $):
  * Best (with prefix caching + aggressive batching): ~1,250K tokens / $1 -> effectively ~$0.0008 per token equivalent
  * Expected (moderate caching, 4-8 request batching): ~850K tokens / $1 -> ~$0.0012 per token equivalent
  * Worst (no caching, single-request latency sensitive): ~420K tokens / $1 -> ~$0.0024 per token equivalent
- Primary drivers: prefix (KV) cache hit rate, average prompt length, batching window and SLO for latency.

MAP milestones (draft):
- 11/09: Delivery of eval prompt set + telemetry hooks (your side)
- 11/14: POC start (1 week) — functional validation + baseline token profile
- 11/21: Pilot start (4 weeks) — cost profiling with caching/batching experiments
- 12/19: Go/no-go review and procurement sign-off

I've attached: Lumexa_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP + milestone dates), token_econ_sensitivity.csv (spread of tokens/$ under scenarios), and a short eval-plan-outline.md. Ben and Neha — please confirm the tokens/$ calc assumptions and flags for caching we should highlight to procurement.

Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Looping in technical clarifications so procurement has defensible language: 

- Caching: our 'prefix' (KV) cache provides savings only when the majority of the prompt (or response) is repeated across calls. For Lumexa's use-case (templated triage prompts with variable patient text) we measured ~35-60% effective prefix reuse in early samples. Use 45% as the conservative expected hit rate.
- Batching: throughput batching helps cost but increases p99 latency. For pilot we can run two profiles: 1) latency-sensitive (batch size <= 2, batching window 25ms) and 2) cost-optimized (batch size up to 8, window 150ms). Expected tokens/$ gains shown in the sensitivity CSV.
- Token counting nuance: embeddings or reranker calls are charged differently—flagged in the spreadsheet. The tokens/$ rows assume generation-only calls.

I'll add a short paragraph to the MAP doc explaining how we translate hit-rate to effective tokens per dollar and include the equations so procurement can validate. Also recommended guardrails: max avg latency for production route, and a canary rollback that disables large-batch mode if SLAs degrade.

-ben
